pages.title: happy birthday
pages.blurb: Happy Birthday on a loop, from a MIDI file, with a second voice that only plays what fits. Shake to bring it in, tilt up for a descant or down for a bass line.

pages.title: sync
pages.blurb: The same rhythm on every device, from the clock alone. Open it on two phones and see how well they agree.

pages.title: thrum
pages.blurb: Sound aimed at the hand, not the ear. Shake for separate taps, turn until they fuse into one buzz, tilt to set the carrier.

pages.title: combo
pages.blurb: Kit, moog bass and piano on one bar. Turn to widen the pitch set, shake to step the rhythm, flick to move the root.

pages.title: marimba
pages.blurb: Struck bars over a bar cut four ways. The octave walks per note, so the figure changes shape with it.

pages.title: dulcimer
pages.blurb: A hammered string walking down three octaves. A finer bar reaches further down the pool.

pages.title: piano
pages.blurb: Six samples, one per octave, and an arpeggio that stretches the wrong one to reach every note.

pages.title: kit
pages.blurb: A half-second bar cut into two, four or eight. Move to change how finely, not how fast.

pages.title: beast
pages.blurb: Five against four against seven. Shake it to drive it, turn it to open the filter, tilt and roll for the timbre.

pages.title: suz
pages.blurb: A nine-note melody against a sixteen-step octave, drifting apart. Move to play, tilt to change register.

pages.title: moog
pages.blurb: Three detuned oscillators through a resonant lowpass. Five against six against two.

pages.title: pluck
pages.blurb: A plucked string you knock to pitch and move to play.

pages.title: train melody
pages.blurb: A five-note figure. Tilt down to raise the octave, roll to sweep the filter against its resonance.

pages.title: multibeat
pages.blurb: A half-second bar cut into one, two or four. Move to change the subdivision, not the tempo.

pages.title: droplet
pages.blurb: Synth droplets. Hold the phone flat to play, stand it upright to stop. Flick it to lengthen the tails.

pages.title: touch
pages.blurb: A strip per note. Press anywhere to sound it, slide up for louder, use as many fingers as you have.
